files.lines: decodeSetSchedParams, cap_sched_context_cap case (~lines 1336-1353)
files.why: The checks reject any sc when the TCB already has a scheduling context (tcb->tcbSchedContext) or when sc->scTcb is set, even if that sc is already this TCB's. They should only fail if tcbSchedContext != sc or sc->scTcb != tcb. The isBlocked/sc_released check should also be skipped when sc is already bound. invokeTCB_ThreadControlSched already tolerates sc == target->tcbSchedContext.

files.lines: decodeSetSchedParams (MCS), case cap_sched_context_cap, ~lines 1336-1353
files.why: The checks reject the call whenever tcb->tcbSchedContext or sc->scTcb is set, so passing the SC already bound to this TCB fails. They should be skipped when sc == tcb->tcbSchedContext (fail only if the TCB is bound to a different SC, or the SC is bound to a different TCB). The invoke function already treats sc == target->tcbSchedContext as a no-op.

files.lines: decodeSetSchedParams, MCS case cap_sched_context_cap (lines ~1336-1353)
files.why: The checks reject any TCB that already has a scheduling context and any SC with scTcb set, so re-binding the same SC fails. They must only fail when tcb->tcbSchedContext != sc or sc->scTcb is a different TCB, and the scNotification binding should also be rejected.

files.lines: VPPIEvent() (lines ~106-135) and VGICMaintenance() (~137-147), the early-return guard
files.why: The guard only checks tcbQueued, so a current thread that is already in the release queue (tcbInReleaseQueue) or lacks a ready, sufficient refill still gets a fault IPC. The reply path then calls postpone() and tcbReleaseEnqueue() a second time and hits the assert.

files.lines: doReplyTransfer() MCS block (~182-195) and postpone() (~569)
files.why: The fault-reply path calls postpone() without checking whether the thread is already in the release queue, so a thread already released-queued gets enqueued twice.

files.lines: VPPIEvent (~line 117) and VGICMaintenance (~line 144)
files.why: The MCS guard only checks tcbQueued, so when the current thread has already been postponed into the release queue (tcbInReleaseQueue, insufficient budget with period != budget) the VPPI/maintenance fault is still delivered and postpone()/tcbReleaseEnqueue runs a second time; the guard must also return when tcbInReleaseQueue is set.

files.lines: VPPIEvent() (~line 117) and VGICMaintenance() (~line 144)
files.why: The MCS guard only tests tcbQueued, so a thread that was just postponed into the release queue (tcbInReleaseQueue, not tcbQueued) still gets handleFault(), which can postpone it a second time and trip the tcbReleaseEnqueue assert; the guard should also return if tcbInReleaseQueue is set or the thread is not schedulable.

files.why: ANSI_DARK emits "\033[30;1m" (foreground black, bold), which is invisible on terminals whose background equals the scheme's black; use bold alone (e.g. "\033[1m") or another non-black/white color.

files.lines: p_tagged_union grammar (~line 229) plus TaggedUnion class: tag_name/tag_offset/tag_size handling, tag enum, tag reader, constructors, field-function generation, and the Isabelle/HOL proof generators (e.g. ~line 753 get_%(tag_name)s)
files.why: This is the only bitfield generator; its parser must accept `tagged_union <type> <field>[:<field>]*` and its code generation must use a combined tag mask, plain-number tag enums, a combined tag read, and no per-field functions for tag fields.

files.lines: SEL4_ARCH_INVOCATION_TEMPLATE (lines ~69-89) and ARCH_INVOCATION_TEMPLATE (lines ~102-122)
files.why: The first label is assigned `= nInvocationLabels` (or `= nSeL4ArchInvocationLabels`) only inside the loop, so with an empty list the terminal `nSeL4ArchInvocationLabels` (or `nArchInvocationLabels`) gets 0; the final enumerator needs an explicit initial value (e.g. `= nInvocationLabels` when no labels exist) or the template must emit it when `first` is still set.

files.lines: p_tagged_union (~229-232); TaggedUnion.__init__/tag checks (~1259-1300); TaggedUnion.generate (~1744-1980, tag enum, get/equals/ptr_get, new/set field skipping, tagmask at ~1906); generate_hol_defs/generate_hol_proofs (~1339-1680); Block field-skipping at ~2612
files.why: The generator only supports a single contiguous `tagname` field, so the parser, the same-position/width validation, the combined tag mask (OR of fields), the tag enum, tag read/equals functions and the omission of tag-field accessors (set etc.) all need extending to a list of tag fields.

files.lines: lines 104-110: ANSI_RESET/ANSI_GREEN/ANSI_DARK macros (and their use in the userError macro at ~138-139)
files.why: ANSI_DARK is "\033[30;1m" (black foreground, bold), which is invisible on dark terminals where black matches the background; it should be bold only or a non-black/white colour.

files.lines: lines 104-110 (ANSI_RESET/ANSI_GREEN/ANSI_DARK macros) and the user of them at ~138-139
files.why: ANSI_DARK emits \033[30;1m (black foreground), which is invisible on dark terminals, and ANSI_GREEN forces a colour; use bold-only or a non-black/white colour (or drop colouring).

files.lines: SEL4_ARCH_INVOCATION_TEMPLATE (lines ~69-89, the `first` handling and `nSeL4ArchInvocationLabels` at line 88); same pattern in ARCH_INVOCATION_TEMPLATE (lines ~102-122, `nArchInvocationLabels`)
files.why: The first label is the only one assigned `= nInvocationLabels`, so with an empty list on ia32 the terminator `nSeL4ArchInvocationLabels` is a plain 0; the template must emit `nSeL4ArchInvocationLabels = nInvocationLabels` when no labels were emitted (and likewise `nArchInvocationLabels = nSeL4ArchInvocationLabels` for an empty arch list).

files.lines: SEL4_ARCH_INVOCATION_TEMPLATE (lines ~61-92, enum sel4_arch_invocation_label, final `nSeL4ArchInvocationLabels` at line 88); also ARCH_INVOCATION_TEMPLATE (~94-125, `nArchInvocationLabels` at line 121)
files.why: The base value (`nInvocationLabels` / `nSeL4ArchInvocationLabels`) is only assigned to the first label inside the loop, so with an empty invocations list (e.g. ia32) the terminating count enumerator defaults to 0. The template must emit the count as `= nInvocationLabels` (or `= nSeL4ArchInvocationLabels` for the arch layer) when no label was emitted, for example by tracking `first` and assigning it explicitly.

files.lines: p_tagged_union (l.229-232) and p_tags/lexer; TaggedUnion class (l.1259+: __init__, resolve, make_classes, generate, generate_hol_defs, generate_hol_proofs, make_names); Block.make_names (l.2612) and Block generate/generate_hol_* where field == union.tagname is suppressed; templates at l.359-480
